title: Values, types and fmt
summary: Declare variables, convert between numeric types explicitly, and format output with fmt.
hints: `Greeting`: an `if name == "" { name = "world" }` followed by `"Hello, " + name + "!"` (or `fmt.Sprintf("Hello, %s!", name)`) is all it takes. Strings compare with `==` in Go.
`Average`: Go never converts numbers implicitly, so `(a + b) / 2` is *integer* division. Convert first: `float64(a+b) / 2`. Then `7` and `8` give `7.5`, not `7`.

`Describe` is a single `fmt.Sprintf("%d = 0x%x = 0b%b", n, n, n)`: `%d` decimal, `%x` hex, `%b` binary. For `ZeroValues`, declare with no initialiser (`var i int`, `var s string`, `var b bool`, `var sl []int`, `var m map[string]int`, `var p *int`) and format them with `"%v %q %v %v %v %v"`.
